title: A Variable Star
text: The Chinese annals record that on Dec. 10, 173 A.D., a brilliant star appeared between Alpha and Beta Centauri in the Southern Hemisphere. It remained visible for eight months, and is described as resembling “a large bamboo mat!”—a curious description. There is at present close to the spot indicated, a known variable star—R Centauri—of which the period seems to be long and the variation of light irregular. Possibly an unusually bright maximum of this variable star formed the star of the Chinese annals, or perhaps the variable star is the remnant of the outburst which took place in the first century. The variable is a very reddish star, and at present varies from about the sixth to the tenth magnitude
